walkthroughs.body_html:
Formulae & Equations — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Formulae & Equations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Formulae & Equations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Sodium has atomic number 11. Its electron configuration is:
An atom of Mg loses 2 electrons to form Mg²⁺. Its number of protons is:
Can a single standard electrode potential be measured in isolation?
options: No — electrode potentials are RELATIVE values measured against a reference (the standard hydrogen electrode, defined as 0 V).
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.
Each electrode has an absolute potential that can be measured directly with a voltmeter.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
